item.title: Ethno-sustainability of an Indigenous Architecture in the Northern Philippines Using Grounded Theory
item.description: This study investigates the ethno-sustainability of Itawit architecture as a distinctive indigenous practice in the Cagayan province of Northern Philippines. Employing a qualitative grounded theory approach, data were gathered through ethnographic interviews, field observations, and archival research with building owners, carpenters, shamans, and elders from Middle and Southern Cagayan. item.title: The Urban Sensory Ambiance of Batroun’s Old Patrimonial Souk in the Face of Overtourism
item.description: The old patrimonial souk of Batroun, in northern Lebanon, is undergoing deep change due to overtourism. Once a center for local trade and crafts, the souk has shifted since the early 2000s toward tourism and commercial entertainment. This change has disrupted its multisensory ambiance, altering how long-term residents perceive, use, and emotionally connect with space. item.title: Landscape of Anonymity: Transforming the Retired COVID-19 Field Medical Facility into A Memorial Park
item.description: During the COVID-19 emergency, the escalating number of cases overwhelmed the admission capacity of operating hospitals in many cities. The pandemic thus prompted the rapid construction of temporary field hospitals in cities like Wuhan, China, to relieve pressure on existing health infrastructure. While their operational phase has been well-documented, the post-pandemic reuse of these facilities remains underexplored. item.title: Comparative Analysis of Informal Vendors around Dhaka Metro Stations through a Sustainable Livelihood Framework
item.description: Dhaka’s urban landscape is undergoing rapid transformation with the introduction of the Metro Rail, reshaping mobility patterns and influencing informal economies. This study investigates how the establishment of Farmgate and Mirpur-10 metro stations has affected the livelihoods of informal vendors, applying the Sustainable Livelihood Framework (SLF) as an analytical lens. item.title: Can Cultural Capital and the Right to the City Explain Class-Based Alienation in Thailand’s Art Museums?
item.description: Contemporary art museums in Thailand often fail to engage working-class communities, revealing a disconnect between institutional narratives and the lived realities of marginalized urban citizens. This study investigates how cultural exclusion reflects broader socio-economic inequality, contributing to the journal’s focus on the economic ramifications of urbanization. item.title: Influence of the Mass Rapid Transit System on Plotted Residential Property Prices: A Case Study of Gurugram, India
item.description: Mass Rapid Transit Systems (MRTS) are increasingly recognised as critical drivers of urban transformation, particularly in rapidly urbanising cities at the Global level. However, empirical research on their influence on plotted residential property markets in emerging urban contexts remains limited. item.title: Advancing Zero-Carbon Cities through Urban Green Infrastructure in Karaj, Iran
item.description: Urban areas in semi-arid regions face rising thermal stress and carbon emissions due to rapid densification and scarce vegetation. This study evaluates the effectiveness of green infrastructure (GI) in mitigating these challenges in District one of Karaj, Iran, within a zero-carbon city framework. item.title: From Connectivity to Liveability: Enhancing Urban Waterbody Accessibility through Space Syntax in Dhaka
item.description: Urban waterbodies play a vital role in enhancing ecological sustainability, social interaction, and neighbourhood liveability, yet in rapidly urbanising contexts such as Dhaka, they are increasingly threatened by encroachment, pollution, and reduced accessibility. item.title: Heritage-Led Urban Regeneration in Rome: Recontextualising the Campo Trincerato through Network Strategies
item.description: Contemporary peri-urban landscapes face fragmentation, marginalisation, and the neglect of widespread cultural heritage. This article explores heritage-led regeneration as a strategic framework to revitalise marginal areas by focusing on the Campo Trincerato in Rome, a system of fifteen forts and three batteries constructed between 1877 and 1891. item.title: Superblock Urbanism in Dhaka as a Sustainable Redevelopment Strategy for Tejgaon Industrial Area
item.description: Dhaka’s rapid urbanisation has intensified challenges of fragmented land use, congestion, and environmental decline, particularly in the Tejgaon Industrial Area (TIA), once designated for light industry but now marked by unregulated mixed-use growth.
